stories.title: Council by-election: nominations require an appointment
stories.summary: Grand Falls-Windsor will elect a councillor on December 1. Nomination day is Monday, November 9, from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. at Town Hall, 5 High Street; prospective candidates must book an appointment at 709-489-0407. Advance voting is November 21. The Town's election page also explains candidate eligibility, voter requirements and proxy voting.
stories.why: A council vacancy is filled by residents choosing a representative. The immediate practical deadline is for prospective candidates; the Town has yet to publish all regular polling locations.

stories.title: Remembrance Day shifts Wednesday garbage collection
stories.summary: Town Hall will be closed Wednesday, November 11, for Remembrance Day and will reopen Thursday, November 12 at 8:30 a.m. Garbage normally collected Wednesday will instead be picked up Thursday, November 12. Thursday's regular collection will also proceed as scheduled.
stories.why: The shift affects Wednesday pickup households; residents should put out waste on Thursday rather than assuming Wednesday service is running.

stories.title: Lincoln Road residential land proposal heads toward public hearing
stories.summary: Proposed amendments would redesignate Lincoln Road recreation open space for low- and medium-density residential use. Two copies of a signed written objection or representation must reach the Town Clerk by 4:30 p.m. on November 16. A public hearing is scheduled for November 18, 6:30–9 p.m., but may be cancelled if no objection is filed.
stories.why: The choice involves housing supply and the future of public open space. Residents can ask how the plan would protect walking connections while accommodating new homes.

stories.title: Highway-twinning land plans leave a ski club seeking answers
stories.summary: The Province has begun expropriating land along the south side of the Trans-Canada Highway for twinning near Grand Falls-Windsor. NTV reported October 29 that a local ski club still lacks answers about what the land acquisition means for its members. No specific trail closure, affected distance or mitigation plan has been verified.
stories.why: Safer highway travel matters, but so does dependable access to the recreation spaces people already use. The immediate question is what the final parcel and corridor plans actually change—and how any disruption could be avoided or mitigated.

stories.title: Red Maple Festival enters its final four days
stories.summary: Grand Falls-Windsor's Red Maple Festival continues through Thursday, November 5. The Town lists a free family movie night at Y2C on Monday, November 2 at 6:30 p.m.; bedtime storytime at Harmsworth Public Library on Tuesday, November 3 at 6:30 p.m.; and a community bonfire at Red Cliff Rocks Campground on Thursday, November 5 from 6–8 p.m. Check the Town's full schedule for other activities and any changes.
stories.why: The festival's Halloween weekend and rescheduled family day have passed. The useful information now is the remaining programme, not expired contests or old event locations. The Town's updated schedule is the authoritative source.

stories.title: Scott Avenue housing consultation has closed; outcome not yet confirmed
stories.summary: The October 28 deadline for written comments has passed on the Town’s proposal to invite multi-unit housing development on Scott Avenue, between Mill Road and Carmelite Road. The published design remains illustrative; the notice does not establish a final Council approval or a developer award.
stories.why: The next meaningful development is a documented Council decision and the terms of any eventual project—not the illustration or the consultation deadline.

stories.title: Province tenders first 6.2 kilometres of highway-twinning work
stories.summary: The Province issued a tender October 22 for 6.2 kilometres of Trans-Canada Highway subgrade work beginning near Grand Falls-Windsor. Future phases remain in design; no contractor award or local subcontracting outcome has been verified.
stories.why: The project could bring procurement opportunities for GFW-based firms, but an issued tender is not evidence of an award or of local economic benefit.
